rulings.challenge_claim: Both original-language disclosures overstate what the bytes give: the ketiv/qere is reported one word too wide, and the plene Jerusalem contrast is drawn against a comparand that does not isolate the plene variable.
rulings.grounds: Both arms are byte-true. MT 26:18 runs מיכיה מִיכָה֙ הַמּ֣וֹרַשְׁתִּ֔י (oshb:Jer.26.18, byte tier): the unpointed ketiv, then the pointed qere, then ordinary pointed text; the note inventory carries exactly one note at that verse, covering one word. The row names מִיכָה֙ הַמּ֣וֹרַשְׁתִּ֔י as the qere, which annexes an unnoted word into the apparatus. Second, the plene site is vav-prefixed, וִירוּשָׁלַ֨יִם֙ (oshb:Jer.26.18, byte tier), while the comparand offered from 25:18 is יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ (oshb:Jer.25.18, byte tier), unprefixed, so the pair varies the conjunction as well as the mater; a same-shape comparand stands in the bytes at וִירוּשָׁלִָֽם (oshb:Jer.27.21, byte tier, also at oshb:Jer.27.20) (sweep: vav-prefixed defective spelling 6 verses; plene spelling 1 verse, this site). Two further defects at the same verse, raised by neither item: the seg inventory carries a paseq at MT 26:18, inside this span, and the row's disclosure sentence speaks only to parashah marks, so the span's seg-layer disclosure is incomplete (count-only, single-witness); and the gloss “Zion will be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem will become heaps” (web:Jer.26.18) is paired with a splice ending at וִירוּשָׁלַ֨יִם֙ that does not contain עִיִּ֣ים תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה (oshb:Jer.26.18, byte tier), so quote and splice are not co-extensive. The seam at 26:17 and the medium_low calibration are untouched; severity is medium on the added findings, not on the challenge as framed, which sits at low.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: cut the qere report to the single word the note covers (ketiv מיכיה against qere מִיכָה֙), leaving הַמּ֣וֹרַשְׁתִּ֔י as ordinary text; replace the 25:18 comparand with the vav-prefixed defective spelling at oshb:Jer.27.20 or oshb:Jer.27.21 so the pair varies only the mater, each spelling carrying a digit-bearing sweep naming object and unit; re-cut the Zion/Jerusalem pairing so the English and the splice are co-extensive (extend the splice through עִיִּ֣ים תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה or shorten the quote to end at Jerusalem). boundary_evidence_refs: add oshb:Jer.27.20 / oshb:Jer.27.21 (and web: counterparts) for the new comparand and drop the 25:18 pair if it is no longer argued. device_notes: add the paseq at oshb:Jer.26.18 as count-only, single-witness. Tests the cure must pass: the qere sentence names exactly the one word the note carries; the spelling pair differs in one variable only; every English quote is byte-verbatim and co-extensive with its paired splice; and every verse argued in prose outside the span appears in boundary_evidence_refs.

rulings.challenge_claim: Each of the row's two pivots turns on a particle it does not weigh: the opening coordinator is byte evidence for the reading the row rejects, and the closing adversative that carries the asserted contrast is left outside the splice while the English reaches wider than the splice does.
rulings.grounds: The first arm is upheld and the second is real but mis-framed. Upheld: the row's own first word is the coordinator וְגַם (oshb:Jer.26.20, byte tier), which is the byte ground for reading 26:20-26:23 as continuing the elders' speech — the very reading the rationale sets aside with the assertion that the case stands on its own footing; a device sitting at the row's own opening seam argues continuity unless it is answered, and strongest_rejected_alternative answers a different rival (splitting off 26:24). Real but mis-framed: the adversative אַ֗ךְ (oshb:Jer.26.24, byte tier) is indeed outside the splice, which begins at יַ֚ד, and it is the one byte carrying the contrast the same sentence asserts — but the added charge that the English reaches wider is byte-false here: the paired quote “the hand of Ahikam the son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah” (web:Jer.26.24) also begins after the adversative, since the verse reads “But the hand of Ahikam” (web:Jer.26.24); gloss and splice are co-extensive and simply start one word late. That charge does land one verse-set earlier in the same row, unraised by either item: “There was also a man who prophesied in Yahweh’s name” (web:Jer.26.20) is paired with a splice ending at מִתְנַבֵּא֙ which does not contain בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.26.20, byte tier). Disclosure is otherwise correct: the petuchah at MT 26:24 is the only inventory entry across 26:20-26:24, with no segs and no notes there. The boundary is untouched.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: extend the 26:24 splice and its paired English one word left so both begin at the adversative אַ֗ךְ, since the contrast asserted in that sentence rests on it; extend the 26:20 splice through בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה so it covers the English paired with it. boundary_rationale or strongest_rejected_alternative (within its two-sentence limit): add one clause weighing the opening coordinator וְגַם as the byte ground for the continuation reading and saying why the participant turn still governs. Tests the cure must pass: every splice is co-extensive with the English quoted beside it; and the row answers the question its own first word raises — which byte at 26:20 argues against this cut, and what answers it.

rulings.challenge_claim: The stated ground for holding Jer.27.1-Jer.27.11 together is byte-refuted — the row denies any fresh discourse imperative in verses 5 through 10 and 27:9 carries one — the closure signal in the row's own last verse goes unquoted, three glosses reach past their splices, and the pre-seam false-prophecy clause recurs past the seam undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: The absence claim fails on the bytes at exactly one of its three limbs. 27:9 opens וְ֠אַתֶּם אַל תִּשְׁמְע֨וּ אֶל נְבִיאֵיכֶ֜ם (oshb:Jer.27.9, byte tier): the fronted second-person plural pronoun, then the negative particle with a prefix-conjugation verb — a directive shape, and the staged extract carries no morphology layer, so it is named by its bytes rather than form-labelled. The shape recurs (sweep: 6 verses book-wide, four in this chapter — 27:9, 27:14, 27:16, 27:17). The row's other two limbs hold: no messenger formula reopens between 27:5 and 27:10 (the chapter's koh-amar sites are 27:2, 27:4, 27:16, 27:19, 27:21) and no addressee changes there, so the one-unit outcome survives — the cure is the stated ground, not the span. The closure device is likewise byte-true and unused: 27:11 carries נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.27.11, byte tier) and the splice stops at וַֽעֲבָד֑וֹ; with a fresh addressee onset at 27:12, closure corroboration is available at this row's own seam and is in neither the quotation nor the declared signals. The three pairing defects are confirmed: at 27:1 the English runs to “this word came to Jeremiah from Yahweh, saying,” (web:Jer.27.1) while the splice ends at מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה; at 27:3 the English carries “to Jerusalem to Zedekiah king of Judah” (web:Jer.27.3) while the splice is only אֶל צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה, not הַבָּאִ֣ים יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם (oshb:Jer.27.3, byte tier); at 27:11 the English carries “that nation I will let remain in their own land,” (web:Jer.27.11) while the splice stops before וְהִנַּחְתִּ֤יו עַל אַדְמָתוֹ֙. The cross-seam recurrence is upheld with its count object corrected: the clause as quoted, כִּ֣י שֶׁ֔קֶר הֵ֖ם נִבְּאִ֣ים לָכֶ֑ם (oshb:Jer.27.10, byte tier), stands in 2 verses — 27:10 inside the span and 27:14 past its close — not 3; the 3-verse figure belongs to the clause taken without the opening particle, whose third site prefixes the noun and so breaks contiguity. Added, unraised by either item: a second formula shape inside the span is unnamed — 27:2 opens כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י (oshb:Jer.27.2, byte tier), the bare shape addressed to the prophet (sweep: bare shape 152 verses; the full stack the row does declare, 32 verses) — and the row's splice of that verse begins after it. The held-open royal-name crux is handled correctly (sweep: defective spelling 1 verse; full spelling 22 verses), the construction is verse-initial as treated, the inventories carry no entry anywhere in 27:1-27:11, and the disclosed petuchah at MT 26:24 checks out. The pairing class recurs at 26:18, 26:20, 27:18, 28:1 and 28:4 among the rows adjudicated here, so its cure is a sweep across the part, not a spot fix.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: restate the one-unit ground to what the bytes support — no messenger formula reopening and no addressee change between 27:5 and 27:10 — and either drop the no-fresh-discourse-imperative limb or disclose the directive at 27:9 and say why it does not cut (it addresses the audience already addressed since the relayed message opened); re-cut the 27:1, 27:3 and 27:11 pairings so quote and splice are co-extensive; extend the 27:11 splice through נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה; add the 27:2 formula shape, named as its own count object with a digit-bearing sweep. observed_substrate_signals: add the closure-formula key for oshb:Jer.27.11 and a key for the bare formula shape at oshb:Jer.27.2. device_notes: disclose the false-prophecy clause recurring past this row's own close at 27:14, citing the swept form and its digit. Tests the cure must pass: no absence claim survives unless a sweep of its own object returns nothing in the span; every English quote is byte-verbatim and co-extensive with its splice; every recurrence digit names the exact form swept and its unit; and the span stays as tiled — this is a rationale and evidence-field cure, not a respan.

rulings.challenge_claim: The addressee turn anchoring this seam is byte-true, but a two-device refrain straddles the seam undisclosed and the ruled closure signal inside the row's own final verse is neither quoted nor listed.
rulings.grounds: The straddle is byte-true at both devices. 27:14, inside the span, carries וְאַֽל תִּשְׁמְע֞וּ אֶל דִּבְרֵ֣י הַנְּבִאִ֗ים and closes כִּ֣י שֶׁ֔קֶר הֵ֖ם נִבְּאִ֥ים לָכֶֽם (oshb:Jer.27.14, byte tier); 27:16, the first verse past this row's close, carries אַֽל תִּשְׁמְע֞וּ אֶל דִּבְרֵ֣י נְבִֽיאֵיכֶ֗ם and כִּ֣י שֶׁ֔קֶר הֵ֖מָּה נִבְּאִ֥ים לָכֶֽם (oshb:Jer.27.16, byte tier). Both devices therefore stand on either side of the row's own closing seam undisclosed, and 27:14 is the one verse of the span the rationale never engages. The count objects want naming: the clause with its opening particle stands in 2 verses (27:10, 27:14) and the pronoun byform in 1 (27:16), while the 3-verse figure belongs to the clause taken without that particle; the directive shape sweeps to 6 verses book-wide, four in this chapter. The closure arm is likewise byte-true: 27:15 opens כִּ֣י לֹ֤א שְׁלַחְתִּים֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.27.15, byte tier) and the splice begins at וְהֵ֛ם, so with a fresh addressee onset at 27:16 the corroboration standing in the row's own last verse is absent from both quotation and signals. Verified sound: both addressee turns are verse-initial and byte-true; the inventories carry no mark, no seg and no note anywhere in 27:11-27:15, as the row states; and this row's three paired quotes are each co-extensive with their splices, so the pairing defect running through its neighbours is absent here. The boundary stands — the defect is disclosure, not tiling.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: disclose the two devices recurring across the closing seam — the negative-listening directive and the false-prophecy clause standing at 27:14 inside the span and again at 27:16 immediately past it — each with a digit-bearing sweep naming the exact form swept (clause with the particle 2 verses; pronoun byform 1 verse; directive 6 verses book-wide, four in this chapter), and state why the addressee turn still governs the seam. boundary_rationale: extend the 27:15 splice left to include כִּ֣י לֹ֤א שְׁלַחְתִּים֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה so the closure formula is quoted, and engage 27:14, the one verse of the span currently passed over. observed_substrate_signals: add the closure-formula key for oshb:Jer.27.15. Tests the cure must pass: no verse inside the span is left unengaged while carrying a device that recurs past the span's own edge; every recurrence citation names the swept form and its unit; and the added quotation stays byte-verbatim and co-extensive with its splice.

rulings.challenge_claim: The declared speech-formula signal names an object that is not the one at the row's own onset, and three distinct formula shapes inside the span are carried under that single label, including the book's full divine stack at 27:21, which is never named.
rulings.grounds: Byte-confirmed at all three sites. The onset formula, inside the row's own opening splice, is bare: כֹּה֮ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֒ (oshb:Jer.27.16, byte tier), with no tsevaot, while the declared signal names the tsevaot object. The span then changes shape twice: כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Jer.27.19, byte tier), and כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Jer.27.21, byte tier), the full divine stack, which is its own count object. The three are distinct objects on the bytes (sweep: bare shape 152 verses; tsevaot shape 50 verses; full stack 32 verses, 31 of them with the koh-amar opener), so one key across all three blends count objects that the semantic-class discipline keeps apart, and the site carrying the book's signature stack goes unnamed anywhere in the row while the rejected alternative reaches only the second site. The continuity conclusion itself survives: the mouth and the addressee do run on from 27:16 through 27:22, so the one-unit ruling is not disturbed — the defect is the signal key and the unnamed object. Added, unraised by either item: the 27:18 pairing is not co-extensive — the English runs the whole verse from “But if they are prophets” to “don’t go to Babylon.” (web:Jer.27.18) while the paired splice is only יִפְגְּעוּ נָא֙ בַּֽיהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Jer.27.18, byte tier). Disclosure is otherwise complete and correctly typed: petuchah at MT 27:18 and MT 27:22, setumah at MT 27:20, the seg at MT 27:18 cited count-only, and MT 27:15 unmarked.
rulings.remedy: observed_substrate_signals: replace the single tsevaot key with keys matching the bytes at their sites — the bare formula for the onset at 27:16, the tsevaot formula for 27:19, and the full-stack key for 27:21. boundary_rationale or device_notes: name the three shapes as distinct count objects, each with its own digit-bearing sweep (bare 152 verses; tsevaot 50 verses; full stack 32 verses, 31 with the koh-amar opener), and state that one mouth and one addressee run through all three, which is what the one-unit ruling rests on. boundary_rationale: re-cut the 27:18 pairing so quote and splice are co-extensive. Tests the cure must pass: every declared signal key matches the byte form at the site it is attached to; no two formula shapes are counted or labelled under one key; and every English quote is byte-verbatim and co-extensive with its splice.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row names the mouth for the opening divine formula but leaves the second divine formula in the same quoted speech unattributed while rendering it in English, and it labels a mid-verse dated construction with an onset key.
rulings.grounds: The first arm is upheld in full and the second needs correcting. Upheld: 28:4 carries נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.28.4, byte tier) mid-verse, inside the same quoted speech whose opening formula the row does attribute; the splice ends at מֶֽלֶךְ יְ֠הוּדָה while the paired English runs the whole verse and renders it as “says Yahweh” (web:Jer.28.4). So a divine formula is reported in English without the mouth-naming the row itself insists on two verses earlier, the pairing is not co-extensive, and the formula standing at the row's own close is absent from the declared signals — with a fresh speaker onset at 28:5, that is exactly the condition under which the ruled treatment makes it available as closure corroboration. Corrected: the positional fact is byte-true — 28:1 carries בְּרֵאשִׁית֙ מַמְלֶ֨כֶת֙ as its fourth and fifth words, after וַיְהִ֣י בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַהִ֗יא (oshb:Jer.28.1, byte tier), against the verse-initial construction at 27:1 (sweep: this spelling 2 verses, 27:1 and 28:1; the two-spelling class 3 verses, adding the other byform at 26:1) — but calling the declared key a mislabel over-reads it: this site is a byte-verified member of that construction class, the dated notice does open the unit, which is what the key asserts, and the row's own splice displays the mid-verse position. What is owed is a per-site position disclosure, not a key change; that arm alone sits at low. Two further defects, unraised by either item: the seg inventory carries a paseq at MT 28:1 and another at MT 28:3, both inside the span, and the row discloses the note at 28:1 and the preceding petuchah at MT 27:22 but neither seg (count-only, single-witness); and the 28:1 pairing is not co-extensive either — the English runs the whole verse, including “in the fourth year, in the fifth month” (web:Jer.28.1), while the two splices offered stop short of the year-and-month phrase and the closing scene clause. The frame-ownership work at 28:2 and the ketiv/qere report at 28:1 are correct and byte-checkable.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: extend the 28:4 splice through נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה and name its mouth as the row already does for the opening formula — the same quoted speech carries both — or shorten the English so no unspliced formula is rendered; add one clause disclosing that the dated construction stands mid-verse here, after the vayehi-bashanah-hahi opening, against the verse-initial site at 27:1, naming the spelling; re-cut the 28:1 pairing so quote and splice are co-extensive. observed_substrate_signals: add the closure-formula key for oshb:Jer.28.4; keep the dated-construction key, which matches the class. device_notes: add the two segs at oshb:Jer.28.1 and oshb:Jer.28.3 as count-only, single-witness, beside the note already disclosed. Tests the cure must pass: no divine formula is rendered in English in this row without its mouth named; every quote is co-extensive with its splice; the mid-verse position claim is readable off the row's own splice; and the span's seg-layer disclosure covers every seg the inventory carries inside Jer.28.1-Jer.28.4.
